nodes.question: Compare the source and edited images: can the original mug be reliably identified, and where is it relative to the headphones in the edited image?
nodes.criteria: Assess the source mug as the object to be moved, not merely any mug-like object in the edited image. Complete only when the source mug is visibly relocated to the right of the headphones. Partial only when the source mug is reliably identifiable and visibly moved rightward from its source position but remains short of being right of the headphones. Absent when the source mug shows no rightward movement. If identity or movement cannot be established, or the evidence is consistent with duplication or erasure rather than relocation, use unknown. Ignore unrelated edits.
nodes.binding: Source image: the light-blue ceramic mug with a handle, left of the black over-ear headphones. Reference: the black over-ear headphones. Track the source mug across the edit; do not substitute another mug-like object.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
